props.title: We Don't Live Here Anymore

sections.content: **We Don't Live Here Anymore** (2004) stands as a razor-sharp dissection of marital infidelity in the tradition of **Scenes from a Marriage** (1973) and **In the Bedroom** (2001). Director John Curran adapts Andre Dubus's short stories with unflinching intimacy, letting Mark Ruffalo and Laura Dern embody the slow-burning devastation of parallel affairs. The film's power lies in its refusal to moralize - instead showing how seemingly stable marriages can unravel through small betrayals and unspoken resentments. Like **Little Children** (2006), it explores suburban discontent with psychological complexity rather than melodrama. We Don't Live Here Anymore|2004|Two married couples' lives implode as they engage in overlapping affairs|Prime Video Closer|2004|Four Londoners destroy their relationships through sexual obsession and betrayal|Netflix The Last Five Years|2014|A marriage dissolves as two artists pursue conflicting dreams|HBO Max

The film's visual style mirrors its emotional claustrophobia. Curran and cinematographer Maryse Alberti keep the camera uncomfortably close to the characters, trapping them in tight frames that echo their spiritual confinement. This technique recalls similar approaches in **Revolutionary Road** (2008) and **Blue Valentine** (2010), where domestic spaces become pressure cookers for festering discontent. The Pacific Northwest setting adds another layer of isolation - rain-soaked woods and gray skies reflecting the characters' moral murkiness.

What elevates **We Don't Live Here Anymore** above typical infidelity dramas is its nuanced portrayal of how affairs impact children and extended social circles. Like **The Ice Storm** (1997), it shows how parental secrets poison family dynamics. Naomi Watts and Peter Krause deliver devastating supporting performances as the other couple, their own marriage corroding through neglect and suspicion. The film's structure, alternating between perspectives, emphasizes how infidelity creates rippling circles of damage. In the Bedroom|2001|A family unravels after tragedy strikes their small Maine town|Paramount+ Blue Valentine|2010|A couple's relationship deteriorates through past and present timeline|Netflix Little Children|2006|Suburban parents begin a dangerous affair amid community tension|HBO Max SUBHEAD: The Literature of Infidelity on Screen

The film's literary origins in Dubus's short stories connect it to a rich tradition of adultery narratives in both literature and cinema. Like **The Age of Innocence** (1993) and **The English Patient** (1996), it treats infidelity as a lens for examining broader social constraints and human nature. The academic setting, with its poetry readings and literary discussions, provides intellectual scaffolding for the characters' moral compromises, similar to how **Wonder Boys** (2000) uses academia to frame its exploration of creative and personal ethics.
